correctness.rationale: RESULT.md 23–69: the squared-modulus normalization gives r in [0,1], with r=1 exactly for equal nonzero moduli. Chebyshev integration by parts gives sign (-1)^(k-1), a strictly increasing absolute coefficient for k>=1 (the derivative factor k+sru is positive), and pairing u,-u gives a strictly decreasing positive mean. The endpoint Rodrigues integrand is proportional to (1-u)^(k-1/2)(1+u)^(s-1/2), integrable. Its beta integral and Gamma duplication give c_k(1)=2^(-s) Gamma(2s+1)/(Gamma(1+s-k) Gamma(1+s+k)); reflection and the Gamma-ratio bound give the stated absolutely summable coefficients and summable domination of the asymptotic series. The regular-polygon Fourier filter therefore applies for every m. Equality requires r=1, all alias cosines at maximal modulus, and no sign cancellation. Making the first alias positive makes the second negative; making the first negative at maximal modulus puts a zero on the grid and makes all aliases negative. At m=1 this gives exactly Q=0 and E=1. CHECKER.py was inspected as finite floating-point corroboration, not needed for the conclusion.

value.rationale: The canonical complex two-mode space and equal circular grid are natural first instances of deterministic L^p discretization. The exact moment constant determines the sharp finite-m error budget (not only an order of decay); the classification identifies a concrete obstruction, an on-grid zero, and the side of the error. This is useful even without an extension to higher dimensions or arbitrary designs.
